{{Quote|Stay strong, Tilden Kaah. With your help&mdash;and with the help of all of us here&mdash;the Keshiri will finish the job. I brought this plague upon us. And I will end it.|Adari Vaal, addressing the Keshiri resistance|<ref name="Paragon" />}}
The '''Keshiri resistance''' was a [[Keshiri/Legends|Keshiri]] movement led by [[Adari Vaal]], dedicated to the removal of the [[Lost Tribe of Sith]] and their control from [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh]] and restoring the authority of the [[Neshtovar]]. In [[4975 BBY]], the resistance group was purged by [[Nida Korsin]]; Vaal and several other members were forced to flee into [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exile]], while the rest were [[Death/Legends|killed]].

==History==
In [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], a group of [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] crash-landed on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh]] and were stranded there. They came into contact with the native [[Keshiri/Legends|Keshiri]], many of whom believed [[Lost Tribe of Sith|the Sith]] to be their [[Deity/Legends|gods]], the [[Skyborn]]. As such, the Keshiri willingly submitted to Sith rule. However, within [[4985 BBY|fifteen years]] of the Sith arrival, many Keshiri&mdash;including [[Adari Vaal]], the Keshiri who had first met the Sith&mdash;had grown very opposed to the Sith presence. As such, they formed the resistance in an attempt to undermine the Sith on Kesh, force them offworld, and free the Keshiri [[Species/Legends|species]].<ref name="Paragon" />

Though the resistance did not organize the [[Red Sith Purge]]&mdash;a purge of all of the [[Sith (species)/Legends|Red Sith]] on Kesh&mdash;they secretly supported it.<ref name="Paragon" /> Ten [[Standard year/Legends|years]] later, in [[4975 BBY]], Vaal prepared the resistance for a [[Keshiri uprising in Keshtah|strike]] against the Sith to weaken their hold on Kesh by stealing their [[uvak]]. However, [[Nida Korsin]], the daughter of [[Grand Lord]] [[Yaru Korsin]], discovered their plans, and foiled them&mdash;many Keshiri in the resistance, including Vaal, were forced into [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exile]], while the rest were [[Death/Legends|killed]].<ref name="Savior" /> The Keshiri species remained indentured to the Sith for millennia, slowly achieving some equality, including the ability for [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] members to join the Tribe.<ref name="Fate of the Jedi: Omen">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Omen]]''</ref>

By [[3960 BBY]], the Keshiri servants told a legend of the flight of the Keshiri resistance, with the moral that it was not their own right to decide their destiny, the right of the Sith to do so. Nevertheless, the [[Sith Saber]] [[Orielle Kitai]] believed that the Keshiri who had fled into exile were the greatest Keshiri who ever lived because they had denied the Sith any such right.<ref name="Lost Tribe of the Sith: Sentinel">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Sentinel]]''</ref>
